prompt: Everyone in the studio comments on the boss design, but only one designer will build and own it.
tells: only one designer will build and own it
why: Let the committed owner decide; others are input.
trap: Opinions are welcome, but the owner decides.

prompt: An executive drops by, suggests a big change, and leaves. The team that will live with it has doubts.
tells: The team that will live with it has doubts
why: The committed team (the pig) should weigh more than a drive-by (the chicken).
trap: Fit may matter too, but the issue is who decides.

prompt: Two leads disagree on a feature. They settle it by asking who will be accountable for it after launch.
tells: who will be accountable for it after launch
trap: It isn't about the vision; it's about ownership.

prompt: A design lead explains: 'For ham and eggs, the chicken is involved, but the pig is committed.'
tells: the chicken is involved, but the pig is committed
why: That's the chicken and pig principle.

prompt: The designer listens to all playtest feedback, but gives the most weight to the engineer who must maintain the system.
trap: Playtesters are fresh eyes, but the decision weighs the committed.

prompt: A lead lets the person who will build a feature make the final call, while coaching rather than dictating.
trap: The lead still guides, but the owner decides.
